title: pack prints a clean good for four questions the kb lacks: tempdb data files, the Microsoft 365 E5 price, Kubernetes Pod Security Admission and Exchange Online retention
goal: rag.py pack no longer prints a clean good (coverage good with no check: and no route: line) for four questions the kb lacks, led by articles on other subjects: the tempdb data file count (security/management-plane-hardening.md), the Microsoft 365 E5 price (windows/bitlocker.md), Kubernetes Pod Security Admission per namespace (arch/k8s-gmsa-windows.md) and Exchange Online retention with Purview (auth/audit-log-apis.md); each prints a check: line or a weak or none verdict, and the eval set keeps its good rows good. Found by the planning probes of SP-j2jn5ue4 (2026-10-12, origin/main 92bc6c598), where DHCP failover and availability group automatic seeding were two more such false goods, which that sprint's research turns into real ones; the pool's sc_absent rows measure the rate.

run:
import subprocess,sys;bad=[]
for q in sys.argv[1:]:
 o=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/rag.py','pack',q],capture_output=True,text=True);t=o.stdout;h=t.split('\n## ')[0]
 clean=t.startswith('coverage: good') and 'check:' not in h and 'route:' not in h;print('clean good' if clean else 'flagged',q);bad+=[q] if clean or o.returncode or not t else []
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

What is the current price of a Microsoft 365 E5 licence?
